full_judgment:
2. The facts leading to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present opposite parties being plaintiffs filed the original Title Suit being No. 12 of 1993 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet contending inter alia, that the predecessors of the plaintiffs namely Ashraf Ali and Md. Asgar Ali had been owned and possessed the suit land after payment of rent regularly. Subsequently the predecessors of the plaintiffs after filing a Title Suit being No. 1002 of 1865 for declaration of title obtained a, decree. Thereafter, due to arrear of rent for some portion of the disputed property it was put into an auction and one Eresh Chandra Dey auction purchased the land and obtained possession therein. The auction purchaser by two registered kabla deeds dated 04-11-1932 AD transferred the land in favour of the plaintiff No. 1's mother Fazira Khatun. The mother of the plaintiff No. 1 along with the predecessors of the plaintiff Nos. 2-5 one Sayab ullah and Nabab ullah purchased some portion of the suit land by a registered kabla dated 14-6-1956 from one Rakesh Ranjan Ghosh and thereby the plaintiffs are possessing the suit land. The further case of the plaintiffs is such that the suit land is not a fishery and in the first part of 1986 AD the plaintiffs for the first time came to know that the suit property has been recorded wrongly in the name of Government as "Dalai Beet". Due to wrong record plaintiff's title to the suit land has been clouded and to dispel the cloud plaintiffs filed the original suit in the court of learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar, Sylhet. 

 3. The contrary case of the defendant-respondent-petitioner government of Bangladesh is such that the disputed property is a "jalmahal" under the government from the very beginning and the kabla deeds in favour of the plaintiff's predecessors dated 04-11-1932 and 14-6-1956 are collusive, forged and created to grab the property The judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 1002 of 1865 is not for the disputed property and the decreetal land of that suit is not identical with that of the present suit properties. The suit properties are fishery in which neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessors allegedly possessed and the record of right in the name of government has been correctly prepared, as "jalmahal" under the government. 

 7. The learned Assistant Attorney General appearing on behalf of the defendant-respondent-petitioner submits that the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity and the impugned judgment and decree is perverse, which suffers from misreading and non-reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Assistant Attorney General further submits that the impugned judgment and decree is against law, facts and evidence on record. The learned appellate court below failed to assess the evidence on record properly in its true perspective and also failed to appreciate the actual position of law. Without reversing the positive findings of the trial court the learned Subordinate Judge, reversed the judgment illegally. The learned A.A.G lastly submits that the disputed property is a "jalmahal" and fishery under the government and the witnesses adduced from the side of the plaintiffs are totally failed to establish the case of the plaintiff-opposite parties which was ignored by the learned lower appellate court during disposal of the appeal and furthermore the witnesses of the plaintiffs are not competent, disinterested and credible and this is the positive findings of the trial court, but in spite of that the learned appellate court decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the plaintiff-appellants arbitrarily without reversing the findings of the trail court considering evidence on record & that's why the impugned judgment is not sustainable in law and facts in respect of the disputed property and that during trial there has been a survey by a survey knowing Advocate Commissioner and the learned Advocate Commissioner by his Report contradicted the case of the plaintiffs and from the Report itself it is clear from the face of the record that suit property is a fishery. 

 8. As against the aforesaid submissions of the learned Assistant Attorney General the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-appellant-opposite parties opposing the Rule submits that the learned appellate court below during disposal of the appeal committed no illegality or irregularity and all the evidence adduced from the sides of the respective parties were properly assessed by the learned Subordinate Judge during disposal of the appeal. The learned Advocate further submits that the witnesses on behalf of the plaintiffs during their deposition before the trial court successfully proved the case of the plaintiffs that the suit land is being possess by the plaintiffs after getting the same from their predecessors in interest. It is also proved that the suit land is not a "jalmahal" or fishery and the settlement record in the name of government is wrong. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the appellate court below after proper sifting of evidence rightly decided the merit of appeal in favour of the plaintiff-appellants and there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree. 

 10. It appears from the case records that the disputed property comprising an area of 10.67 acres appertaining to Mouza Madhurai under Upazila Balaganj of District Sylhet stands in JL No. 232 and Khatian No. 1. The portion of suit land measuring an area of 5.68 acres lies in plot No. 14/135 and in plot No. 21 the area of suit land is 4.99 acres. It is the case of the plaintiffs that they acquired the land by two registered deeds dated 04-11-1932 and 14-6-1956. Admittedly during S.A. Record the land has been recorded as 'jalmahal' under the government in its khash Khatian No. 1 and it is the contention of the plaintiffs that the property is not a 'jalmahal' rather cultivable land and 'boro' corps are being produced therein. 

 11. On careful scrutiny over the papers on record it has come to the notice of the court that in respect of the suit properties there has been a survey by a survey knowing advocate and the learned Advocate Commissioner after holding commission submitted his Report marked as Exhibit-'X'. The learned Advocate Commissioner Mr. Abdul Rashid in his testimony as witness No. 4 states at a stage that he could not relay the land of deed dated 04-11-1932 AD as the plaintiffs could not produce the same before him. Obviously; it is the pleading of plaintiffs that they obtained the disputed property by two kabla deeds of the year 1932 and 1956 and by the kabla deed of the year 1932 they acquired 10 kedars out of suit property and by the remaining deed of the year 1956 they acquired 10 kedars of suit land. The learned trial court during disposal of the original suit opined that the plaintiff no. 1 in his averment states that the area of land is 36/37 kedars. In respect of the identity of the disputed property; on going through the original plaint it is apparent that the plaintiffs in their pleading specifically states to the effect that they acquired the land measuring 10 kedars + 10 kedars = 20 kedars by two registered deeds which was purchased by the mother of the plaintiff no. 1, Fazira Khatun and the predecessor of the remaining plaintiff Nos. 2-5 one Soyabullah and Nababullah. 

 15. The witness No. 3 is Aftab Ali. This witness also states at a stage of his deposition that he does not know the disputed property correctly and he has no land contiguous to the suit land. He also cannot say the plot numbers of the suit property. The solitary witness adduced from the side of the defendant is one Abdur Razzak, who is a Tahsilder and this witness states in support of the case of the government.
